tagline.en: From a model that runs to a service that survives rush hour: optimization, high-concurrency serving with vLLM, multi-GPU, Kubernetes and LLMOps — measured every week on a public leaderboard.

audience.en: ML / LLM engineers, MLOps, DevOps and backend engineers

format.en: 15 topics · each one a lecture + a hands-on seminar

workload.en: ≈ 10–14 hours per week, ≈ 150–200 hours in total

goal.en: Train an engineer who can optimize an LLM, stand up a high-performance OpenAI-compatible API on vLLM, serve dozens to hundreds of concurrent clients from a single instance, deploy the system on multiple GPUs and Kubernetes, and operate it as LLMOps.

outcomes.en: Explain where inference time and memory go — prefill vs decode, the KV cache, memory bandwidth — and predict the bottleneck before measuring it.
Quantize a model and defend the speed / memory / quality trade-off with numbers.
Serve a model through vLLM's OpenAI-compatible API and tune it for a given concurrency profile.
Benchmark a serving stack honestly: throughput, TTFT, TPOT, p95, failures — under 1 to 128+ concurrent clients.
Package, deploy and scale inference: Docker, tensor parallelism, Kubernetes with GPU Operator and HPA.
Operate it: metrics, dashboards, alerts and cost per million tokens.

prerequisites.en: Python — confident; asyncio basics help (we write load generators).
Linux command line and git — you will ship a repository every week.
Deep-learning basics — what a transformer forward pass and a token are; PyTorch at the reading level.
HTTP / REST basics — requests, JSON, streaming responses.
Accounts: GitHub, Hugging Face, Google (for Colab). No prior Docker or Kubernetes needed — taught in the course.

judge.en: The instructor's workstation · 1 × NVIDIA RTX 5070 Ti (Blackwell, 16 GB GDDR7)

devBox.en: Google Colab (free tier: NVIDIA T4, 16 GB)

modelRule.en: Any open-weight model that, together with its KV cache for 64 concurrent requests, fits in 16 GB of VRAM. Your choice — and it may change between rounds.

stackRule.en: Any stack and any kernels: vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, TensorRT-LLM, your own CUDA/Triton — as long as the contract holds.

submission.en: Push a git tag round-NN to your public repository before the round deadline (TBA). The judge checks out exactly that tag.

role.en: model id, stack, key parameters, author
installs pinned dependencies with uv and starts an OpenAI-compatible server on :8000, model name "submission"
pinned environment — the run must be reproducible from a clean machine
one entry per round: what changed, why, what it measured — the raw material of your defense
optional — if present, the judge uses it instead of serve.sh

speed.en: Output tokens/s at concurrency 32 and 64, plus p95 TTFT — GuideLLM on a fixed, hidden prompt set.

quality.en: A gate, not a score: a subset of GSM8K, MMLU-Pro and IFEval through lm-eval against your endpoint. Below the gate → the round counts as failed.

ranking.en: Among submissions that pass the quality gate, rank by speed.

marks.en: Each round is marked 0–5. Clearing that round's speed bar = 5. The bar rises from round to round (baseline of the round + x%). Exact bars and the partial-credit formula: TBA with the leaderboard spec.

overdrive.en: Top 10% of a round: +2 Overdrive points. Next 10%: +1. Overdrive does not inflate the 40% — it buys exam exemption.

exemption.en: Overdrive ≥ N (TBA) by the end of round 10 → the final exam is waived and credited at 80% (40 / 50).

dryRun.en: Every week the judge publishes a dry-run log, so you can see your submission start on Blackwell before it counts.

note.en: Covers all 15 topics, including multi-GPU and Kubernetes. Can be waived through Overdrive.
Mandatory. The engineering story of your solution: every change, why, and what it measured.

policy.en: Cheating — zero tolerance. No late submissions: a missed round deadline is a 0 for that round. Gaming the benchmark (caching eval answers, special-casing the prompt set, degrading output to win speed) disqualifies the round.
